questions.question: What does 'a cold fish' mean?

options.A: an unfriendly person who hides their feelings
options.B: a person who loves cold weather

questions.correct_answer_text: an unfriendly person who hides their feelings

steps: 'A cold fish' is an idiom for an unfriendly person who does not show emotions.
solution.summary: a cold fish = an unfriendly person.

questions.explanation: The idiom 'a cold fish' describes someone who seems cold and distant.

questions.question: What does 'a dark horse' mean?

options.A: a person with hidden ability who is not well known

questions.correct_answer_text: a person with hidden ability who is not well known

steps: 'A dark horse' is an idiom for someone who keeps their abilities secret and surprises others.
solution.summary: a dark horse = someone with hidden ability.

questions.explanation: A dark horse seems quiet but turns out to be surprisingly able.

questions.question: What does 'a go-getter' mean?

options.A: an energetic, ambitious person who works hard to succeed
options.B: a person who gets lost easily
options.C: someone who takes things too quickly
options.D: a person who gives up easily

questions.correct_answer_text: an energetic, ambitious person who works hard to succeed

steps: 'A go-getter' is an energetic and determined person who tries hard to succeed.
solution.summary: a go-getter = an ambitious, hard-working person.

questions.explanation: A go-getter is active and determined to achieve success.

questions.question: What does 'a mover and shaker' mean?

options.A: an important person with power and influence
options.B: a person who works out at the gym

questions.correct_answer_text: an important person with power and influence

steps: 'A mover and shaker' is an idiom for an important, influential person.
solution.summary: a mover and shaker = an influential person.

questions.explanation: Movers and shakers are people who have power and influence in an organisation.

questions.question: What does 'a smart alec' mean?

options.A: a person who annoyingly shows off their cleverness
options.B: a person who is intelligent and kind
options.D: a person who tells good jokes

questions.correct_answer_text: a person who annoyingly shows off their cleverness

steps: 'A smart alec' describes someone who is irritatingly eager to show how clever they are.
solution.summary: a smart alec = an annoying know-it-all.

questions.explanation: A smart alec keeps showing off their knowledge in an annoying way.

questions.question: What does 'a smart cookie' mean?

options.D: a person who makes quick decisions

steps: 'A smart cookie' means a clever, intelligent and sensible person.
solution.summary: a smart cookie = a clever person.

questions.explanation: The idiom 'a smart cookie' is a compliment meaning someone is smart.

questions.question: What does 'a soft touch' mean?

options.A: a person who is easy to persuade to give money or help
options.B: a person who is gentle to touch
options.D: a person who avoids contact with others

questions.correct_answer_text: a person who is easy to persuade to give money or help

steps: 'A soft touch' is a person who is easily persuaded, especially to lend money or help.
solution.summary: a soft touch = someone easy to persuade.

questions.explanation: A soft touch finds it hard to refuse requests for money or help.

questions.question: What does 'a social butterfly' mean?

options.A: a friendly person who enjoys spending time with many people
options.C: a shy person who avoids parties
options.D: a person who talks about insects

questions.correct_answer_text: a friendly person who enjoys spending time with many people

steps: 'A social butterfly' is a very sociable person who loves being with lots of people.
solution.summary: a social butterfly = a very sociable person.

questions.explanation: A social butterfly moves easily among many people and enjoys social events.

questions.question: What does 'keep yourself to yourself' mean?

options.A: to be private and not mix with other people
options.B: to keep your own secrets from yourself
options.C: to take care of your own health

questions.correct_answer_text: to be private and not mix with other people

steps: 'Keep yourself to yourself' means to stay private and avoid mixing with others.
solution.summary: keep yourself to yourself = stay private.

questions.explanation: People who keep themselves to themselves avoid socialising much.

questions.question: In the quiz, 'I want to make sure that I am playing to my strengths' means the person ...

options.A: wants to use the things they are good at

questions.correct_answer_text: wants to use the things they are good at

steps: 'Playing to your strengths' means making the most of your abilities.
solution.summary: playing to your strengths = using your abilities.

questions.explanation: If you play to your strengths, you focus on what you do well.

questions.question: A quiz answer says: 'I'm a bit thin-skinned and not competitive, so I'll pass.' This means the person ...

options.A: is easily hurt and does not like competing, so refuses
options.C: will take part because they enjoy challenges
options.D: has no opinion about the quiz

questions.correct_answer_text: is easily hurt and does not like competing, so refuses

steps: 'Thin-skinned' means easily upset and 'not competitive' means not liking to compete, so the person refuses.
solution.summary: The person refuses because they are easily hurt and not competitive.

questions.explanation: The answer 'I'll pass' shows the person does not want to take part.

questions.question: In the quiz answer 'I know that deep down I'm a go-getter', the phrase 'deep down' means ...

options.B: at the bottom of a sea

steps: 'Deep down' means in one's true or real feelings, hidden underneath.
solution.summary: deep down = in your true feelings.

questions.explanation: Saying something is true deep down means it is what you really feel inside.

questions.question: Complete: 'A personality test is a 1 ______ questionnaire created by psychologists.'

steps: The correct word is 'personal' — a personal questionnaire.
solution.summary: A personality test is a personal questionnaire.

questions.explanation: Psychologists create personal questionnaires used in the job process.

questions.question: Complete: 'It is used by companies to help them in their 2 ______ process.'

steps: The correct word is 'job' — the job (hiring) process.
solution.summary: Companies use the tests in their job process.

questions.explanation: Personality tests help companies choose candidates during the job process.

questions.question: Complete: 'The test is usually presented by a 3 ______ or an online platform.'

steps: The correct word is 'speaker'.
solution.summary: A speaker presents the test.

questions.explanation: A personality test is presented by a speaker or an online platform.

questions.question: Complete: 'A 4 ______ person fills it in.'

steps: The correct word is 'quiz' — a quiz person fills it in.
solution.summary: A quiz person fills in the questionnaire.

questions.explanation: The person taking the test fills in the questionnaire.

questions.question: Complete: 'Then, a 5 ______ reads the answers and gives the results.'

steps: The correct word is 'interviewer'.
solution.summary: An interviewer reads the answers.

questions.explanation: After the test, an interviewer reads the answers and gives the results.

questions.question: Which of these phrases is used to CHECK that you have understood someone?

source.reference: Speaking box: Paraphrasing what you hear

steps: 'In other words ...' restates what someone said to check understanding.
solution.summary: In other words = checking understanding.

questions.explanation: The phrases 'In other words', 'If I'm hearing you correctly' and 'Let me get this straight' check understanding.

questions.question: Which phrase from the Speaking box would you use to restate an idea in a different way?

source.reference: Speaking box: Paraphrasing what you hear

steps: 'To put it another way' introduces a paraphrase of what someone said.
solution.summary: To put it another way = restating differently.

questions.explanation: This phrase shows you are re-expressing an idea in different words.

questions.question: Which phrase means you want to confirm that what you understood is correct?

options.C: So, what it boils down to is ...

source.reference: Speaking box: Paraphrasing what you hear

steps: 'If I'm hearing you correctly' is used to check your understanding of what was said.
solution.summary: If I'm hearing you correctly = checking understanding.

questions.explanation: This phrase politely checks that you understood the speaker correctly.

questions.question: Which phrase is used to check understanding before repeating what someone said?

source.reference: Speaking box: Paraphrasing what you hear

steps: 'Let me get this straight' introduces a question that checks your understanding.
solution.summary: Let me get this straight = checking understanding.

questions.explanation: You use this phrase to confirm the facts before continuing.

questions.question: Which phrase below is used to check understanding?

source.reference: Speaking box: Paraphrasing what you hear

steps: 'So you're saying (that) ...' checks that you understood the speaker's meaning.
solution.summary: So you're saying (that) = checking understanding.

questions.explanation: This phrase repeats the other person's point to confirm it.

questions.question: Which phrase would you use to SUMMARISE what someone has said?

source.reference: Speaking box: Paraphrasing what you hear

steps: 'In a nutshell' introduces a short summary of the main points.
solution.summary: In a nutshell = summarising.

questions.explanation: You use 'In a nutshell' to give a brief summary of what was said.

questions.question: Which of the following phrases is used to SUMMARISE rather than to check understanding?

source.reference: Speaking box: Paraphrasing what you hear

steps: 'Simply put' introduces a summary in simple terms.
solution.summary: Simply put = summarising.

questions.explanation: 'Simply put', 'Essentially', 'In a nutshell' and 'boils down to' are summarising phrases.

questions.question: Complete: '______ , what it boils down to is that the test is not reliable.'

source.reference: Speaking box: Paraphrasing what you hear

steps: The phrase is 'So, what it boils down to is that ...' — a summarising expression.
solution.summary: So, what it boils down to is ... = summarising.

questions.explanation: This expression summarises the essential point of what was said.

questions.question: Which of these phrases would you use to introduce a summary of the main idea?

source.reference: Speaking box: Paraphrasing what you hear

steps: 'Essentially' introduces the main, essential point of what was said.
solution.summary: Essentially = summarising.

questions.explanation: You use 'Essentially' when giving the key point in short.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is a point IN FAVOUR of using psychometric tests?

options.A: It's better to know as much about a candidate as possible.
options.B: If a candidate is nervous, they may not perform well.
options.C: People may do badly in the tests.
options.D: It can be expensive to administer and mark the tests.

questions.correct_answer_text: It's better to know as much about a candidate as possible.

steps: Knowing as much as possible about a candidate supports the use of tests.
solution.summary: In favour: more information about the candidate.

questions.explanation: The other options list drawbacks of psychometric tests.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is a point IN FAVOUR of psychometric tests?

options.A: They are usually quick and easy to do.
options.B: A candidate may know what the interviewer wants to hear.
options.C: They can be expensive to administer.
options.D: Candidates may do badly in them.

questions.correct_answer_text: They are usually quick and easy to do.

steps: That tests are quick and easy is given as a positive point.
solution.summary: In favour: quick and easy.

questions.explanation: The other statements present reasons against using the tests.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is a point AGAINST using psychometric tests?

options.A: A nervous candidate may not perform well in an interview.
options.B: It's better to know as much about a candidate as possible.
options.D: They give a fair chance to quiet candidates.

questions.correct_answer_text: A nervous candidate may not perform well in an interview.

steps: That a nervous candidate may not perform well is a drawback of the tests.
solution.summary: Against: nervous candidates may do badly.

questions.explanation: Nervousness could cause good candidates to fail, so this argues against the tests.

questions.question: Which of the following is a point AGAINST relying on psychometric tests?

options.A: People may do badly in them.
options.C: They are quick and easy to do.
options.D: They give a lot of useful information.

questions.correct_answer_text: People may do badly in them.

steps: That people may do badly in the tests is a reason against relying on them.
solution.summary: Against: people may do badly.

questions.explanation: If capable people can fail the tests, the tests are not reliable.

questions.question: Which of the following is a point AGAINST psychometric tests?

options.A: The candidate may know what the interviewer wants to hear.
options.B: They are usually quick to do.
options.C: They reveal more about the candidate.

questions.correct_answer_text: The candidate may know what the interviewer wants to hear.

steps: If the candidate can guess what the interviewer wants, the test result is less reliable.
solution.summary: Against: candidates may give expected answers.

questions.explanation: Candidates might answer what they think the interviewer wants rather than truthfully.

questions.question: Which of the following is a point AGAINST psychometric tests?

options.A: It can be expensive to administer and mark the tests.
options.B: They are quick and easy to do.
options.C: They help choose the best candidate.

questions.correct_answer_text: It can be expensive to administer and mark the tests.

steps: The cost of administering and marking the tests is a drawback.
solution.summary: Against: they can be expensive.

questions.explanation: Companies may find the tests costly to run and mark.

questions.question: According to the discussion statements, what is described as unusual?

options.A: someone leaving school without a career idea
options.B: a candidate feeling nervous in an interview
options.C: a candidate doing badly in a test

questions.correct_answer_text: someone leaving school without a career idea

steps: One statement says it is unusual for someone to leave school without a career idea.
solution.summary: It is unusual to leave school with no career idea.

questions.explanation: The statement questions how common it is to finish school without an idea of a career.

questions.question: In the listening, 'For many people, the word 1 ______ has negative associations.'

steps: The psychologist says the word 'personality tests' has negative associations for many people.
solution.summary: The word is 'personality tests'.

questions.explanation: Many people see personality tests as gimmicky or pseudo-scientific.

questions.question: In the listening, the psychologist says the results are not ______ .

steps: The talk says 'it is not 3 ______ - the results are not fixed'.
solution.summary: The results are not fixed.

questions.explanation: Test results can change over time.

questions.question: In the listening, 'an individual's job ______ can change over time.'

steps: The talk says an individual's job performance can change over time.
solution.summary: Job performance can change.

questions.explanation: Test results and job performance are not permanent.

questions.question: In the listening, what can also affect the results of a personality test?

steps: The talk says an individual's mental and physical health can also affect the results.
solution.summary: Mental and physical health affect the results.

questions.explanation: Changes in life and health can change test results.

questions.question: In the listening, 'No one is hired on the basis of a ______ personality test alone.'

steps: The talk says no one is hired on the basis of a single personality test alone.
solution.summary: No one is hired on one test alone.

questions.explanation: Employers should use a combination of methods, not a single test.

questions.question: In the listening, what is 'always best' according to the psychologist?

steps: The talk says 'a combination of methods is always best'.
solution.summary: A combination of methods is always best.

questions.explanation: Recruiters should combine several methods to judge candidates.

questions.question: What should people in recruiting consider as crucial to performance?

steps: The talk says 'The working environment is crucial to performance'.
solution.summary: The working environment is crucial.

questions.explanation: Recruiters should also consider the working environment.
